summary: Tested merchant login (JWT), access control, admin merchant accounts, the merchant delivery report CSV and the UI flows at 390x844. Backend: 15 of 16 new tests pass, and all 19 tests in the updated iteration-10 regression file pass. The one failure is a security issue: the 5-fails lockout can be bypassed by sending a spoofed X-Forwarded-For header. The full report flow was verified end to end: import for mer-1, batch, start, deliver with signature, rate 4 stars. The CSV row has status=delivered, delivered_at, proof_types=signature, a working https proof_link (200) and rating=4 with its comment. Store-A token on the store-B URL returns 403, a bad token or a session token returns 401, and an invalid range returns 400. UI: all requested flows pass (sign-in errors, redirect to own store, mer-2 to mer-1 redirect, session kept after reload, sign-out, report range chips, download calling window.open with a valid report URL, admin sign-in rejecting merchant credentials, create account, reset password, admin all-stores list, CSV upload, fix-row sheet). Driver, customer and admin consoles still open without login. Deprecated packages detected: none.

critical.issue: The lockout can be bypassed. The key is email + the FIRST X-Forwarded-For entry, which the client controls (the ingress appends the real IP after it). After 5 fails, a request with 'X-Forwarded-For: 9.9.9.9' returns 401 instead of 429, so rotating that header gives unlimited guesses. Fix: use the LAST (ingress-appended) XFF entry, or X-Real-IP, or also keep a per-email counter. Reference: server.py:1922

minor.issue: CSV/formula injection. Customer-controlled cells (rating_comment, customer_name, address, notes) are written raw, so a comment like '=HYPERLINK(...)' runs as a formula in Excel or Sheets. Prefix cells that start with = + - @ \t \r with a single quote; phone numbers like +1415... need care. Reference: server.py:2063-2067

This GET has side effects and N+1 queries: share_proof() runs per delivered stop and may write or rotate share tokens. Downloading a report re-issues expired proof links, which silently kills the old links. Reference: server.py:2058-2059

No authentication, and it wipes all stops, imports and routes, including merchant orders. Now that merchants have accounts, anyone can erase their data. Consider requiring admin_user. Reference: server.py:706

The range filter uses delivered_at or created_at. A still-pending order created more than 7 days ago, or one scheduled for today but created earlier, drops out of the today/7d reports. Consider also using the service date or window_date.
The failure counter never expires (no rolling window). 5 typos spread over weeks still trigger a 15-minute lock.

integration_issues.issue: window.open() is called after an awaited fetch, so the user gesture is gone. Chromium allowed it in testing, but Safari/iOS web usually blocks such popups. Fix: open a blank window synchronously in onPress, then set its location, or use an anchor download. Reference: src/components/ReportDownload.tsx:26

issues: At 390x844 the REMOVE / SAVE & RETRY buttons are below the fold when the sheet opens, so the user has to scroll inside the sheet to reach them. Consider a sticky footer.
The hero image shows a FedEx-branded truck, which is a third-party trademark in a MultiDrop app. Use an unbranded van image.
The red 'MULTIDROP / OPS V1' kicker over the dark photo has low contrast.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the login lockout bypass via spoofed X-Forwarded-For (server.py:1922). Use the trusted last hop or X-Real-IP, and/or add a per-email limit.
Escape formula-leading characters (= + - @ tab CR) in report CSV cells to prevent CSV injection (server.py:2063).
Protect POST /api/admin/reset with admin_user, since it wipes merchant orders.
ReportDownload: open the window synchronously in the press handler so Safari/iOS web doesn't block the popup.
Optional: stop rotating proof share tokens inside the report GET; consider a sticky action footer in FixRowSheet; replace the FedEx-branded hero image.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2298 lines (more than 700) and should be split into modules (auth, merchants/import, report, routes, stops).
Report token lives in the URL query (5 min, purpose=report). That's acceptable, but it isn't re-checked against a disabled or deleted user.
Session is stored in AsyncStorage (localStorage) on web. That's fine for a preview, but note the XSS exposure.
Login correctly uses a dummy bcrypt hash for unknown emails (timing equalised), returns a generic 401, and strips password_hash and _id from responses.

The FixRowSheet retry button needs a mouse wheel scroll inside the sheet before clicking. Viewport 390x844.
rca_of_issue: Lockout bypass: login() builds its key from request.headers['x-forwarded-for'].split(',')[0]. Kubernetes ingress appends the real client IP, so index 0 is whatever the client sent. Reproduce: 5 bad logins for a throwaway email, then a 6th with the header X-Forwarded-For: 9.9.9.9 returns 401 instead of 429. Mitigation: take the last XFF entry (trusted proxy hop) or X-Real-IP, and add a per-email counter that ignores IP.
